title: Direct impact of commonly used dietary emulsifiers on human gut microbiota
authors: Naimi S, Viennois E, Gewirtz AT, Chassaing B
population: Human faecal microbiota maintained in the MiniBioReactor Array model, 3 reactors per condition
funder: European Research Council Starting Grant ERC-2018-StG-804135; Chaire d'Excellence from IdEx Université de Paris (ANR-18-IDEX-0001); Innovator Award from the Kenneth Rainin Foundation; Marie Sklodowska-Curie Individual Fellowship; NIH grants DK099071 and DK083890. Funders had no role in the design of the study and data collection, analysis, and interpretation, nor in manuscript writing.
authorConflicts: The authors declare that they have no competing interests.
result: Of 20 emulsifiers tested, carboxymethylcellulose (E466) and polysorbate 80 (E433) altered microbiota composition without reversal after exposure; polysorbate 80 also altered the metatranscriptome. Carrageenans and gums altered density, composition and expression of pro-inflammatory molecules. Soy lecithin (E322) and mono- and diglycerides did not alter the measured parameters; sunflower lecithin altered alpha diversity only. Faecalibacterium fell with polysorbate 80, iota carrageenan, hydroxypropyl methylcellulose and mono- and diglycerides according to the Discussion; the Results text names polysorbate 80, iota carrageenan, agar agar and DATEM. Three of the products are listed as E471 in Table 1: mono- and diglycerides (Modernist Pantry), glyceryl stearate and glyceryl oleate (Lonza). All faecal samples came from one healthy donor; emulsifiers were added at 0.1% to the medium from 72 to 216 h. Glyceryl stearate increased bacterial density in the treatment and post-treatment phases, caused a non-reversible decrease in evenness, increased bioactive lipopolysaccharide significantly in the post-treatment phase and altered the metatranscriptome; Table 2 classes its effects as non-reversible. Glyceryl oleate caused an irreversible decrease in bacterial density and no other change.
